chapters.1.summary: The book opens by stating its purpose: to teach wisdom, justice, and good sense. The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge. A parent tells a son to listen to his father and mother. Sinners will invite him to ambush the innocent and share the loot. He must not go with them. They set a trap for their own lives. Then Wisdom calls aloud in the street like a woman. Those who refuse her will eat the fruit of their own choices.
chapters.2.summary: The teacher tells his son to accept his words and store up his commands. He must turn his ear to wisdom and call out for understanding. He must seek it like silver and search for it like hidden treasure. Then he will understand the fear of the LORD. The LORD gives wisdom and guards the path of the just. Good sense will protect the learner from men who speak twisted things. It will protect him from the unfaithful wife. The upright will remain in the land.
chapters.3.summary: The teacher tells his son to keep kindness and truth close. He should trust the LORD with all his heart, not his own insight. He should honor the LORD with his wealth. The LORD corrects those he loves, as a father does. Wisdom is worth more than silver and is a tree of life. The learner must not hold back good from one who is owed it. He must not tell a neighbor to come back tomorrow. He must not plot against a neighbor who lives trustingly beside him.
chapters.4.summary: A father tells his sons to listen and gain understanding. He says he was once a tender son himself. His own father taught him to get wisdom above all else. He warns against the path of the wicked. The path of the righteous is like dawn that grows to full day. The learner must guard his heart, for life flows from it. He must keep his mouth honest and his eyes straight ahead. He must make his path level and not turn aside.
chapters.5.summary: The teacher warns his son about another man’s wife. Her lips drip honey, but the end is bitter. Her steps lead down to death. He must stay far from her door. Otherwise strangers will take his strength and wealth, and he will groan at the end. He should drink water from his own well. He should rejoice in the wife of his youth. A man’s ways are before the LORD, and his own sins bind him.
chapters.6.summary: The teacher warns against pledging to cover another person’s debt. If the son has done so, he must free himself at once. He tells the lazy person to watch the ant. She has no ruler and still stores food in summer. A little extra sleep brings poverty like a robber. A troublemaker winks and stirs up quarrels. The LORD hates seven things, including lying and shedding innocent blood. Adultery is like carrying fire in one’s lap.
chapters.7.summary: The teacher tells his son to treat wisdom as a sister. Then he describes what he saw from his window. A young man without sense walked near a certain woman’s corner at dusk. She came out dressed to attract him and seized and kissed him. She said she had made offerings and prepared her bed with fine linen. Her husband was away on a long journey. He followed her like an ox going to slaughter. Her house is the road to the grave.
chapters.8.summary: Wisdom calls out on the heights and at the city gates. She speaks to all people and says her words are true. She is better than silver, gold, and rubies. By her kings rule justly. She loves those who love her. The LORD had her at the beginning, before the mountains and the seas. She was beside him when he marked out the earth’s foundations. Whoever finds her finds life.
chapters.9.summary: Wisdom has built her house with seven pillars. She has prepared meat and wine and set her table. She sends her maids to call from the high places. She invites the simple to come in and eat. The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom. Folly is a loud woman who sits at her door. She calls to the simple with the same words. She offers stolen water, and her guests are in the grave.
chapters.10.summary: Here the short sayings of Solomon begin. A wise son makes his father glad. Wealth gained by wrong does no good. Lazy hands make a person poor, and hard work brings wealth. Love covers all wrongs. Where words are many, sin is not far away. The lips of the righteous feed many people. When the storm passes, the wicked are gone, and the righteous stand.
chapters.11.summary: A false scale is hateful to the LORD, and honest weights please him. Pride brings shame, and humility brings wisdom. A city rejoices when the righteous do well. A gossip reveals secrets, and a trustworthy person keeps them. Many advisers bring safety. One person gives freely and gains more. Another holds back and becomes poor. People curse the one who hoards grain.
chapters.12.summary: Whoever loves correction loves knowledge. A worthy wife is her husband’s crown. A righteous person cares for the life of his animal. The one who works his land has bread. A fool thinks his own way is right. Rash words cut like a sword, and a wise tongue heals. Truthful lips last forever. Worry weighs a heart down, and a kind word makes it glad.
chapters.13.summary: A wise son accepts his father’s teaching. The one who guards his mouth guards his life. Some pretend to be rich and have nothing. Wealth gained in haste shrinks away. Hope put off makes the heart sick. Whoever walks with the wise becomes wise. A poor person’s field may yield much food, and injustice sweeps it away. A parent who loves a child corrects him.
chapters.14.summary: A wise woman builds her house, and a foolish one tears it down. A way may seem right to a person and end in death. Even in laughter the heart may ache. The simple believe everything, and the careful watch their steps. The poor are shunned even by neighbors, and the rich have many friends. Whoever oppresses the poor insults their Maker. A calm heart gives life to the body. Righteousness lifts up a nation.
chapters.15.summary: A gentle answer turns away anger, and a harsh word stirs it up. The eyes of the LORD are in every place. A little with the fear of the LORD is better than great treasure with trouble. A meal of vegetables with love is better than rich meat with hatred. Plans fail without advice. A word spoken at the right time is good. The LORD hears the prayer of the righteous. Humility comes before honor.
chapters.16.summary: People make plans in their hearts, and the answer comes from the LORD. A person’s ways seem pure to him, and the LORD weighs motives. Honest scales belong to the LORD. Pride goes before destruction. Pleasant words are like honey. Gray hair is a crown of glory. One who controls his temper is better than one who captures a city. The lot is cast, and its every decision is from the LORD.
chapters.17.summary: A dry crust with peace is better than a house full of feasting with strife. The LORD tests hearts as fire tests silver and gold. Whoever mocks the poor insults their Maker. One who covers an offense seeks love. A friend loves at all times. To clear the guilty and condemn the innocent are both hateful to the LORD. A cheerful heart is good medicine. Even a fool seems wise when he keeps silent.
chapters.18.summary: A person who keeps apart seeks only his own desire. A fool takes no pleasure in understanding and only airs his opinions. The name of the LORD is a strong tower. A rich man imagines his wealth is a high wall. To answer before listening is folly and shame. The first to state a case seems right until the other side questions him. Death and life are in the power of the tongue. Some friends stay closer than a brother.
chapters.19.summary: It is better to be poor and honest than a liar and a fool. Zeal without knowledge is not good. Wealth brings many friends, and a poor person loses the one he has. A false witness will not go unpunished. Good sense makes a person slow to anger. Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD. People make many plans, and the LORD’s purpose stands. A lazy person will not even lift his hand to his mouth.
chapters.20.summary: Wine is a mocker, and whoever is led astray by it is not wise. It is an honor to stay out of a quarrel. A person’s purpose is like deep water, and a wise one draws it out. No one can say his heart is fully clean. The LORD hates unequal weights and measures. A buyer says “It’s no good” and then boasts of his bargain. Do not say you will repay evil. Wait for the LORD.
chapters.21.summary: A king’s heart is in the LORD’s hand like a stream of water. The LORD weighs hearts. Doing what is right and just pleases him more than sacrifice. The plans of the careful lead to plenty. Whoever ignores the cry of the poor will cry and not be heard. Justice brings joy to the righteous. The sacrifice of the wicked is hateful. The horse is made ready for battle, and victory belongs to the LORD.
chapters.22.summary: A good name is better than great riches. The rich and the poor have this in common: the LORD made them both. Train a child in the way he should go. The borrower is servant to the lender. A generous person is blessed, for he shares his bread with the poor. Then a new set of sayings begins. Do not rob the poor or crush the needy in court. The LORD will take up their case.
chapters.23.summary: At a ruler’s table, the learner must control his appetite. He should not wear himself out to get rich, for wealth flies away. He should not eat with a stingy host. He must not move old boundary stones or take orphans’ fields. Their Redeemer is strong. He should listen to his father and not despise his mother when she is old. The chapter ends with a picture of a drunk person. He is beaten, feels nothing, and wants another drink.
chapters.24.summary: Do not envy evil people or wish to be with them. A house is built by wisdom. If you give up in a hard time, your strength is small. Rescue those being led away to death. You cannot say you did not know, for God weighs hearts. A righteous person falls seven times and rises again. Do not rejoice when your enemy falls. The teacher passes a lazy man’s field and learns from its thorns.
chapters.25.summary: These are more sayings of Solomon, copied by the men of King Hezekiah. God’s glory is to hide a matter, and a king’s is to search it out. Do not push yourself forward before a king. Do not rush to court against a neighbor. A fitting word is like gold apples in a silver setting. A soft tongue can break a bone. If your enemy is hungry, give him food. A person without self-control is like a city with broken walls.
chapters.26.summary: Honor does not suit a fool, like snow in summer. An undeserved curse does not land. Do not answer a fool by his folly, or you will be like him. Answer a fool by his folly, or he will think himself wise. A proverb in a fool’s mouth is useless. The lazy person says a lion is in the road. A meddler in another’s quarrel grabs a dog by the ears. Without wood a fire goes out, and without gossip a quarrel ends.
chapters.27.summary: Do not boast about tomorrow. Let another person praise you, not your own mouth. Wounds from a friend can be trusted. A neighbor nearby is better than a brother far away. As iron sharpens iron, one person sharpens another. A person is tested by the praise he receives. Know the state of your flocks, for riches do not last. The lambs will clothe you, and the goats will feed your household.
chapters.28.summary: The wicked run when no one chases them, and the righteous are bold. A poor man who oppresses the poor is like rain that ruins the crop. It is better to be poor and honest than rich and crooked. Wealth built on high interest ends up with someone kind to the poor. Whoever hides his sins does not prosper. Whoever confesses and leaves them finds mercy. One who hurries to get rich will not go unpunished. Whoever gives to the poor will lack nothing.
chapters.29.summary: A person who is often corrected and stays stubborn will suddenly break. When the righteous increase, the people rejoice. A king builds up the land by justice. The righteous care about justice for the poor. A fool lets out all his anger. The poor and the oppressor both receive sight from the LORD. Where there is no vision, the people cast off restraint. Fear of people is a trap, and trust in the LORD keeps one safe.
chapters.30.summary: These are the words of Agur. He says he is too ignorant to know the Holy One. Every word of God is tested and true. He asks God for two things before he dies. He wants lies kept far away. He wants neither poverty nor riches, only the food he needs. If full, he might deny the LORD, and if poor, he might steal. The chapter then gives lists of things that come in threes and fours.
chapters.31.summary: These are the words King Lemuel’s mother taught him. A king must not waste his strength or dull his mind with wine. Otherwise he will forget the law and wrong the afflicted. He must speak for those who cannot speak. He must judge fairly and defend the poor and needy. A poem then praises a capable wife. She buys a field, trades, clothes her household, and gives to the poor. Charm and beauty pass, and a woman who fears the LORD is praised.
